forecaster_note: Head to overhead at the exposed banks but mostly wind-affected — smaller, cleaner AM options and maybe OK again late PM. A new S swell (7.3ft @ 9s from 180°) is delivering head-to-overhead sets at the south-facing magnets, with waist-to-chest waves at the less exposed breaks, plus an easing ENE swell (3.4ft @ 8s from 68°) in the mix. Winds go light-to-moderate SW early for clean to cleanish surf, though the south exposures stay more wind-affected. Breezy S'lies then add chop to most spots until later PM when the wind eases and things should tidy up. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline Sydney Regional Forecast

wind.summary: SSW 7 km/h gusting 13 at dawn — light and manageable, offshore at Manly, cross at Dee Why, straight onshore at Long Reef and Curly. Swings S and freshens through the morning, so the clean window is early.

days.label: Today
days.note: Real swell in the water — 7.3ft @ 9s from a dead 180° S, with 3.4ft @ 8s ENE underneath. The S angle is why Long Reef and Curly are the biggest and the messiest; it also means Dee Why is wrapping rather than lining up. Wind is only 7 km/h SSW at dawn and freshens S through the morning, so everything worth having is before about 9am. Manly is the one spot with genuine offshore.

dee-why.window: 6:20–8:30am on the push to the 7:43am high. Light SSW cross-shore, workable size. Deteriorates as the S'ly fills in mid-morning.
alerts: Dead S at 180° — the angle that wraps badly here. Expect the bay to be closing out and the Point to be doing the work
S'ly freshens through the morning and adds chop

tip.label: Frontside at the Point — but only the Point
tip.text: The 3.4ft ENE at 68° sits right in your 30–80° sweet spot and is the component that actually gives the Point rights a shoulder. The 7.3ft S at 180° is size without direction here — it wraps and shuts down the bay. Sit up at the Point, go frontside, use the incoming tide before 7:43am. Energy and consistency weren't published this run, so judge it off the cam before committing.

long-reef.window: Dawn only, 6:20–8am, and only if you want the size. Straight onshore SSW and getting worse from mid-morning.
alerts: Biggest of the four — 6–8ft on a raw 9s S swell
Onshore SSW from the start; this is size before shape

tip.label: Most size, least shape
tip.text: The reef is a straight S magnet, so it's converting the full 7.3ft. But onshore SSW on a 9s period means it'll be moving and lumpy rather than lined up. You're a strong paddler and it's within your range, but on a Thursday morning the risk/reward is poor next to Manly.

curl-curl.window: 6:20–8am. Classic Curly S-swell magnet size, but onshore from the outset.
alerts: Onshore SSW — chop on the faces early, worse as the S'ly builds
Strong sweep likely with 7.3ft of S swell running the bank

tip.label: S-swell magnet doing its thing
tip.text: Curly eats S swell, which is exactly why it's 5–7ft when Manly is 4–5ft. North Curly corner will hold the best shape with a bit of protection. Expect a solid rip — pick a bank and keep re-lining.

manly.window: 6:20–9:30am — the longest clean window of the four. Offshore SSW, incoming tide to 7:43am.
alerts: Smallest of the four, but the only one genuinely groomed

tip.label: The pick of the four today
tip.text: North Steyne is the only spot with true offshore SSW, and 4–5ft chest-to-head with a light breeze is the most rideable combination on offer. Less raw S energy reaches here, which today is a feature not a bug. Backside on the lefts along North Steyne, frontside on the Queenscliff-end rights.
